reason: r24 writes the transform's x scale, which r23's run pinned as the reason the clip has no width. The mask's rectangle is built by the game: its enter handler (main+0xa4ba94) rebuilds +0xb0..+0xbc from the node's quad whenever bit 1 of +0xa4 is set, and the quad comes from main+0xa4b390, which composes x = (+0x40) + (+0x20)*yExtent + (+0x10)*xExtent + (+0x30) and y = (+0x44) + (+0x24)*yExtent + (+0x14)*xExtent + (+0x34). r23's run read the rectangle as 110 38 110 70 with authored 128x32 and anchors 0xfffffff0: the authored height contributed 32, the authored width contributed nothing, and the origin came from the parent's transform (110,38, the row root's own origin) while the plugin's position writes were inert. So the width row at mask+0x10/+0x14 is (0,0), the factory's matrix template having no x scale. r24 writes 1.0f at +0x10 and 0 at +0x14, sets the authored pair to (ratio width, the bar's rect height), keeps the anchor clear from r23 (bits 0-3 of +0xa0, mode 3 collapsing an axis, the factory leaving those bits as the allocator handed them), drops the inert position writes, and asks for the game's rebuild and apply (+0xa4 = 3). The probe now logs every input the builder reads, next to the bar's same fields. The insertion has completed four times (r18, r20, r22, r23) with the 5-word object array through the cGUIInstance DTI's MT allocator, the draw block resized through the root's vtable slot 0x58 with main+0xa49b28's arithmetic, the class factory's object, and the native linkers; r22's walker liveness check fired once and re-armed. Quests are split into areas with a loading screen between them (the tester's account of 2026-10-24). Not approved for distribution; r12 and r13 were packaged and never run.
runtime_test: NOT RUN: r24 writes 1.0f at mask+0x10, the transform row the game multiplies the authored width by, and sets the authored height to the bar's rect height. r23 ran on Eden 2026-10-24 (installed bytes 909dd7fa281cc8863c79fef6d91b49cd5ecd2da837ee30ad6d5ed01f7befc225): the anchor clear read back as anchors=0xfffffff0 and all 14 clip lines still showed a zero width at the parent's origin. r22/r20/r18/r14 each completed an insertion and hid the gauge. r17/r16/r15 ran clean.

r2 was built and never run; r3 was run once on Eden and is recorded.
r14 was run once on Eden and failed as reported: the gauge was clipped away from the insertion and the game crashed at the quest end. Its log is the evidence, and the insertion is removed in r15.

r15 was run once on Eden and drew the gauge normally for 740 seconds with no exception; its facts line printed tree_nodes 3 against 4 objects, and its object-list fields were read from the wrong object (the controller's owner field), which is what r16 fixes.

r16 changes nothing on screen: it reads game memory and logs. No drawing, no gauge change, and no cleanup claim (the root-destructor hook fired zero times in the three sessions that logged it). Its Eden run ended in Eden's own shutdown records (maxwell_3d Critical asserts, ForceStop, host SIGSEGV) with zero guest exceptions.
the game's destructor is assumed to free the map block r17 publishes through the cGUIInstance DTI's MT allocator; that free has not been observed, and r17 frees the old 4-word block itself
The per-weapon tier tables live in RomFS weapon data and are not read in this workspace: no weapon data file is extracted here.
The gauge itself is not part of r4.

r24 has not been run. Five completed insertions (r14, r18, r20, r22, r23) have hidden the gauge; r23 proved the anchor clear lands and that the transform's x row is the width's missing input, and no run has read mask+0x10 back.
